speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and weakness in your upper limbs; could you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if they are getting worse?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest is very characteristic. Can you tell me if you experience any difficulty with swallowing or speaking, and do your eyelids droop when you are tired?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since you have no bulbar symptoms like dysphagia or dysarthria, I need to confirm if your double vision is strictly binocular and whether you have experienced any specific triggers for your symptoms. REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR antibodies; REQUEST TEST: Anti-MuSK antibodies.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
